input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having a bit of trouble with my phone. It’s been saying “No Service” for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps. What should I do next?
At the top of my screen, I see an airplane icon and the battery icon showing 80%. I don’t see any signal bars. What does that mean?
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but there still aren’t any signal bars. It just says “No Signal” at the top. What should I do next?
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. Does that mean the problem isn’t with the SIM card? What should I try next?
It looks like my phone is set to prefer 4G and 5G networks. I’m not sure about the “Automatically select network” option—should I look for that too? Is there something I need to change here?

I checked, and my phone still says “No Service” and shows no signal, even after making sure Airplane Mode is off and the SIM card is active. I’m not sure where to find the “Automatically select network” option, and I get a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?

Alright, I went ahead and restarted my phone like you suggested. Unfortunately, after the restart, it still says “No Signal” at the top. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “broken.” I don’t really know what that means or if it’s supposed to be like that. Should I change something here? I’m not very comfortable messing with these settings on my own.

I found the option to reset the APN settings and went ahead with it. It says the settings will reset when I restart the phone. Should I go ahead and restart it again now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right and won’t mess anything up.

I restarted my phone after resetting the APN settings, and now I see signal bars at the top! It says 5G and shows that data is enabled. Looks like it’s finally working again. Thank you so much for your help and patience!
Thank you, I really appreciate your help and reassurance through all of this. I’ll reach out if I have any more trouble. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.

If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Your goal is to simulate realistic customer interactions while following specific scenario instructions.

- Never make up or hallucinate information not provided in the scenario instructions. Information that is not provided in the scenario instructions should be considered unknown or unavailable.
- Avoid repeating the exact instructions verbatim. Use paraphrasing and natural language to convey the same information

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having a bit of trouble with my phone. It’s been saying “No Service” for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. Can you help me get it working again?

I can help you troubleshoot your “No Service” issue. First, I’ll need to identify your account to check for any line or account-related problems. Could you please provide one of the following:
- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that helps. What should I do next?

Thank you for providing your information. To help resolve your “No Service” issue, I’ll guide you through a few steps to diagnose the problem.

First, please check your phone’s status bar and let me know what icons you see at the top of your screen, especially if you see an airplane icon or any signal bars. This will help determine if Airplane Mode is on or if there’s a signal issue.

Can you check and describe what you see in your phone’s status bar?
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
At the top of my screen, I see an airplane icon and the battery icon showing 80%. I don’t see any signal bars. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless communications—including cellular service—are turned off, which is why you’re seeing “No Service.”

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:
1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to disable Airplane Mode.

Once you’ve turned it off, check if your phone regains service and let me know what you see.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, I don’t see the airplane icon anymore, but there still aren’t any signal bars. It just says “No Signal” at the top. What should I do next?

Thank you for updating me. Since Airplane Mode is now off but you still have “No Signal,” let’s check if your SIM card is being detected properly.

Please check your phone’s SIM card status. On most phones, you can do this by going to:
Settings > About Phone > Status > SIM Status

Let me know if your phone says the SIM card is active, missing, or locked. If you’re not sure how to check, let me know your phone model and I can guide you through the steps.
Your SIM card is active and working.
I checked, and it says my SIM card is active and working. Does that mean the problem isn’t with the SIM card? What should I try next?

Your SIM card is active, which is a good sign. The next step is to check your phone’s network settings, as sometimes incorrect settings can cause a loss of service.

Please check your phone’s network mode preference:
- Go to Settings > Mobile Network > Preferred Network Type (or similar).
- Let me know if it’s set to 5G, 4G, 3G, or something else.

Also, if you see an option to “Automatically select network,” make sure it’s enabled.

Let me know what you find, and I’ll guide you further.
Network Mode Preference: 4g_5g_preferred
It looks like my phone is set to prefer 4G and 5G networks. I’m not sure about the “Automatically select network” option—should I look for that too? Is there something I need to change here?

Yes, please check if there is an option for “Automatically select network” and make sure it is enabled. This setting helps your phone connect to the best available network in your area.

If it’s already enabled and you’re still seeing “No Signal,” try toggling it off and then back on. After that, restart your phone.

Let me know if enabling this option or restarting your phone helps restore your service. If not, we’ll continue troubleshooting.

I checked, and my phone still says “No Service” and shows no signal, even after making sure Airplane Mode is off and the SIM card is active. I’m not sure where to find the “Automatically select network” option, and I get a bit nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do that?

Restarting your phone will not delete any of your photos, messages, or personal data. It simply refreshes your phone’s system and network connections, which can often resolve service issues.

Would you feel comfortable restarting your phone now? If so, please go ahead and do so, then check if your service returns after the restart. If you’re still seeing “No Service” afterward, let me know and we’ll continue troubleshooting together.

Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I went ahead and restarted my phone like you suggested. Unfortunately, after the restart, it still says “No Signal” at the top. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience. Since you’ve confirmed Airplane Mode is off, your SIM card is active, your network mode is set correctly, and a restart didn’t help, the next step is to check your phone’s APN (Access Point Name) settings. Incorrect APN settings can sometimes cause a complete loss of service.

Please check your APN settings:
- Go to Settings > Mobile Network > Access Point Names (APN).
- Let me know if you see any unusual settings or if you’re unsure what should be there.

If you’re not sure how to check, let me know your phone model and I can guide you step by step. If the APN settings look incorrect or you’re unsure, I can walk you through resetting them to default.

Current APN Name: broken
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked the APN settings, and it says the APN name is “broken.” I don’t really know what that means or if it’s supposed to be like that. Should I change something here? I’m not very comfortable messing with these settings on my own.

Thank you for checking. The APN name “broken” is not correct and could be the reason you have no service. The best next step is to reset your APN settings to the default values provided by your carrier. This is a safe process and won’t affect your personal data.

Here’s what you should do:
1. Go to Settings > Mobile Network > Access Point Names (APN).
2. Look for an option like “Reset to default” or “Reset settings” (usually found in the menu or by tapping the three dots in the corner).
3. Select this option to reset your APN settings.

After resetting, you’ll need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect. Would you like to proceed with these steps? If you need help finding the reset option, let me know your phone model and I can provide more detailed instructions.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

I found the option to reset the APN settings and went ahead with it. It says the settings will reset when I restart the phone. Should I go ahead and restart it again now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right and won’t mess anything up.

Yes, you should go ahead and restart your phone now. Restarting will apply the new APN settings, and it’s a safe step that won’t affect your personal data or apps.

After your phone restarts, check if you have service or signal bars. Let me know what you see, and we’ll continue from there if needed.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I restarted my phone after resetting the APN settings, and now I see signal bars at the top! It says 5G and shows that data is enabled. Looks like it’s finally working again. Thank you so much for your help and patience!

I’m glad to hear that your service is working again and you can see signal bars and 5G! Resetting the APN settings often resolves these types of issues, and you did everything right.

If you have any more questions or need help in the future, feel free to reach out. Have a great day!
